about: The evangelium of the formulary “Dedication of Saint Michael the Archangel” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, the disciples approached Jesus, saying: Who, do You think, is the greater in the kingdom of heaven? And Jesus called to Him a little child, stood him in the midst of them, and said: Amen I say to you, unless you are converted and become as little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven. Whoever, then, humbles himself like this little child, he is the greater in the kingdom of heaven. And whoever welcomes one such little child in my name welcomes me. But whoever leads one of these little ones who believe in me into sin, it is better for him that a millstone turned by a donkey be hung on his neck, and that he be sunk in the depths of the sea. Woe to the world because of occasions of sin. For it is necessary that occasions of sin come; but woe to that man through whom the occasion of sin comes. But if your hand or your foot leads you into sin, cut it off and throw it from you; it is better for you to enter into life crippled or lame than to be cast into eternal fire with two hands or two feet. And if your eye leads you into sin, pluck it out and throw it from you; it is better for you to enter into life one-eyed than to be cast into the Gehenna of fire with two eyes. Take care not to despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven.

a.g: For occasions of sin must come
